idiom_name: log/slog.Handler chaining crypto/hmac over the appended record
implementation_notes: The standard library supplies both halves: log/slog.Handler is the chokepoint - Handle(ctx, Record) receives the record after WithAttrs/WithGroup have resolved the context - and crypto/hmac plus crypto/sha256 produce the authenticator. A chaining handler keeps prev and seq as fields, serialises the record once with a canonical key order, and writes those exact bytes through an io.Writer opened with O_APPEND; the hand-rolled logger is only justified below Go 1.21 or when the bytes must match an existing verifier exactly.
pitfalls: slog.Handler must be safe for concurrent use and WithAttrs returns a derived handler: keeping chain state in a derived copy rather than in shared state produces several chains writing one file.
Hash exactly the bytes you store: if the handler chains a canonicalised copy but the sink writes the original record, the verifier will disagree with the file even when nothing was tampered with.

A Handler error surfaces only through the Logger that owns it (and slog ignores it in several configurations) - wire an explicit policy, because silently dropped audit records are indistinguishable from deleted ones.
